html:
Aristotle was a Greek philosopher and scientist, born in Stagira in northern Greece in 384 BCE, who studied and taught in Athens. His writings on logic, nature, ethics and politics framed learning in Europe and the Islamic world for about two thousand years.

He spent some twenty years as a student at Plato's Academy. He then tutored the young Alexander at the court of Macedon, and in 335 BCE opened his own school in Athens, the Lyceum. When Alexander died in 323 BCE, anti Macedonian feeling in Athens drove him out, and he died the next year.

Unlike Plato, he looked for truth in the world as it is, by collecting and sorting facts.

  • Logic: he set out the syllogism, the first formal system of reasoning.
  • Biology: he described and classified hundreds of animals, many from his own observation.
  • Ethics: in the Nicomachean Ethics the good life is a life of virtue, built by habit.
  • Politics: he compared the constitutions of Greek cities and called man a political animal.

His physics, with its heavy earth at the centre of the cosmos, was wrong, and it took the Scientific Revolution to overturn it. His works passed through Arabic scholars such as Averroes back into Latin Europe, where Thomas Aquinas joined them to Christian theology.
